item.title: Carney enlists fake Trump for laughs at Canada's annual press gallery dinner
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with a fake Donald Trump and two versions of himself Saturday, enlisting comedians to help roast the U.S. president and Canadian politicians at an annual dinner with journalists

item.title: Amtrak train derails after striking truck in Louisiana
item.description: "All passenger cars remained upright," Amtrak said.

item.title: Ligue 1: Marseille lose to Le Mans after being two goals up at home
item.description: Olympique de Marseille suffered a home defeat against Le Mans (3–2). Having led 2-0 after 40 minutes thanks to goals from Gouiri (33’) and Paixão (40’), OM collapsed.

item.title: Woman at center of Nvidia scandal was in touch with China's top spy agency: Sources
item.description: Alice Huang was in contact with an official at China’s Ministry of State Security, officials said.

item.title: Live: Zelensky confirms Ukraine’s military struck Russian ships in Libyan waters
item.description: Ukraine’s military was responsible for drone attacks on two Russian vessels at the Libyan port of Benghazi Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Monday. The president alleged that the Russian corvette Merkury had been sunk in the attack. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Concertgoer describes 'distressing scenes' after 'unknown substance' released
item.description: A concertgoer has described "really distressing scenes" after more than 12,000 people were evacuated from the UK's biggest arena when an "unknown substance" was released.

item.title: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey’s crackdown on opposition and media
item.description: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday against a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media, days after police raided Sozcu TV and arrested senior staff. The main opposition Yeni Parti organised the protest after authorities installed a government-appointed trustee at the broadcaster, following similar moves against other independent outlets.

item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
item.description: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible. (Image credit: John Minchillo)

item.title: Christmas market returns to Paris' Champs Elysées
item.description: France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet reports from the opening of the Paris Christmas market on the Champs Elysées.

item.title: France's far-right leader Le Pen denies receiving secrets from civil servant
item.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen Sunday denied receiving confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party, while acknowledging she could not say whether others in the party had benefited.

item.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapse
item.description: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is taking place amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the war in Iran.

item.title: Drone strikes hit homes, United Nations building in Sudan's capital
item.description: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.

item.title: Major trial to examine if AI can help detect breast cancer earlier
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of women taking part in the NHS breast cancer screening programme could have their scans assessed by AI to see if it leads to earlier diagnosis.

item.title: Russian ship attacked near Benghazi in suspected drone attack
item.description: Authorities in divided Libya's east said a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port was hit on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

item.title: Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
item.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism”. Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister ⁠Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

item.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
item.description: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.

item.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
item.description: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

item.title: Burnham, 'Brejoin' & the Ghosts of Brexit
item.description: “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.

item.title: Man charged with raping woman on Brighton beach
item.description: A 28-year-old man has been charged with raping a woman on Brighton beach in the summer.

item.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
item.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.

item.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
item.description: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked. (Image credit: Mohammed Yassine for NPR)

item.title: Rahm Emanuel: Schumer should commit to stepping down as leader after next Congress
item.description: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, joined "This Week" to discuss what Democrats should do after their historic midterm victory.

item.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
item.description: From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex, a new book of short stories written by kids who are part of the "Read Alex" literacy program in Johannesburg. Participants in weekly classes wrote stories drawing on their own lives.'/> South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors. (Image credit: Madalene Cronje for NPR)

item.title: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury
item.description: A bittersweet victory for PSG at Nice on Saturday evening. The Parisians strengthened their grip on top spot in Ligue 1, but lost Désiré Doué for several months after the forward suffered a serious knee injury.

item.title: Drone strikes hit homes and UN building in Sudan's Khartoum
item.description: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.

item.title: DNI Clayton: Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'
item.description: The director of national intelligence appeared on ABC's "This Week" Sunday.

item.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
item.description: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming. (Image credit: Khalil Hamra)

item.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
item.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

item.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
item.description: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.

item.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
item.description: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: 'It can take years': Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
item.description: Artificial intelligence claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.

item.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
item.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.

item.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot. (Image credit: Joe Cavaretta/South Florida Sun Sentinel)

item.title: Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
item.description: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.

item.title: Suspect charged over death of man found injured in hospital car park
item.description: A suspect has been charged following the death of a young man who was found seriously injured in a hospital car park, almost 20 miles from where he was wounded.

item.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
item.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.

item.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
item.description: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

item.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare
item.description: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost. (Image credit: Philip Cheung for NPR)

item.title: NPR's Senior Podcast Challenge: Early entries we love
item.description: People 65 and older have been submitting stories for a chance to win our grand prize — a visit to NPR watch your podcast air live on Weekend Edition . There's still time to enter!
